newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA SPINNERS KEEP ENGLAND IN CHECK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA SPINNERS KEEP ENGLAND IN CHECK.

text.p: Spinners Shane Warne and Michael Bevan picked up three top order wickets shortly before tea to keep England in check on the second day of the third test at Old Trafford on Friday.
After Australia were dismissed for 235, England were 110 for four at the interval.
It was another twist in a fascinating match, pegging England back just as they had moved into a strong position.
After skipper Michael Atherton was caught behind for only five, Surrey team mates and brothers-in-law Mark Butcher and Alec Stewart pushed the score slowly to 74 for one.
Then Warne struck twice in five overs, luring Stewart (30) and Graham Thorpe (three) into nicking catches to Mark Taylor at slip.
In between, Bevan's left-arm spin brought the wicket of Butcher for 51 with his sixth ball. Healy brought off a brilliant leg side stumping to register his 100th dismissal in Ashes matches.
The spinners' success took some of the heat off Taylor, whose decision to bat first in much more difficult conditions after winning the toss had been widely criticised.
Australia had earlier resumed at 224 for seven but added only 11 runs for the loss of their remaining three wickets, which fell in eight-and-a-half overs.
Darren Gough picked up two of them, bowling Paul Reiffel for 31 and then Steve Waugh for 108, an innings that Waugh felt was as good as he had played in test cricket.
Dean Headley dropped a sharp caught-and-bowled chance from Jason Gillespie then had him caught behind for a duck next ball to give wicketkeeper Stewart six catches.
Headley's reward for an impressive debut was bowling figures of four for 72.
